differences.what: massing: a narrow, tall stone town house, its front flat, attached on the north to the Farwell house and open to the south, its south side wall receding along the open ground; the draft stood a grey mansard box 6.75 m wide
differences.how: T-2432: K01 frontage on the 1911 sheet's plan at the trace's own 7.6 m width; the front's two edges land within 3 px of the photograph's (x 140 and 433), the south wall recedes on the camera's solve

differences.what: storey lines and the north part's windows: three storeys, the ground floor near grade; ground-floor lights 1.1-2.7 m over grade, first-floor 4.15-6.4 m, second-floor 7.8-10.1 m, two a storey in the north part
differences.how: T-2432: a 0.45 m ground floor and 3.15, 3.6 and 3.8 m storeys; the north part's sills and heads fall within about 5 px of the photograph's, their columns within about 8 px

differences.what: the entrance at grade at the south end of the front, flat-headed, reached by two low steps, with one window a storey over it
differences.how: T-2432: the K07 door at front bay 5.75 m, three 0.15 m risers; its jambs within 5 px of the photograph's

differences.what: the gable: the photograph carries the whole front up as a steep coped WALL GABLE, about 57 degrees, its apex about 18.8 m over grade, three segment-headed lights in the attic at 11.6-13.4 m and an oculus near the apex; the build has a 45-degree slated hip and a single-light pedimented dormer on the front's centre line, its light at the gable lights' height and its apex about 4 m lower
differences.how: T-2435, with T-2428's K01 wall gable

differences.what: the south side wall's eave: the photograph's runs about 13 m over grade, a knee wall under the attic; the build's eave is the third floor's, 11.0 m

the windows' kind: the photograph's ground- and first-floor windows are leaded casements, two lights under a transom, mullioned, in dressed quoined surrounds; its second-floor windows single one-over-one sash under segmental heads, the middle one standing a little south of the windows under it; the build has K06 two-over-two sash under flat stone lintels, all on one bay line

the frontispiece: the front's south part stands slightly proud, its edges quoined; the photograph has a carved panel over the door, a four-light mullioned and transomed window over it under a hood mould and two narrow segment-headed lights above that; the build has one sash a storey in that bay
the base: the photograph shows a plain plinth with no basement lights; the build has low area lights under the ground-floor windows, which a K01 front without its own openings row must carry
the stacks: the photograph's tall stack stands on the north party wall near the front, beside the gable; the build's stands 9.4 m behind the front (a K01 stack may not stand in the dormer's body)

the four-storey rear section: the photograph shows it stepping out to the south behind the main body under a mansard with a dormer and a stack, as the 1911 sheet traces it (s20-1625-a1); not built, a K01 rear wing standing only behind the main body inside its width
the picket fence along the open ground to the south, and the builders' stone and barrels on the walk
differences.how: the fence is the lot's, not the house's, and is not built here; the debris is the photograph's day in 1889

differences.what: colour and tone: the photograph is monochrome; its stone reads mid-grey and rock-faced, the south wall's brick lighter
differences.how: the stone is K02's brownstone on the Tribune's 'red stone' (quoted by chicagology, not yet a source record); L-k01-1625-mcbirney-tudor-2432
